title: Client Review done twice
summary: One consulting engagement (case for the client identified in the log) went through the Client Review stage twice within about two weeks — first on 2026-05-04 with one consultant, then again on 2026-05-18 with a different consultant. Both review entries ended in the same unresolved state, 'awaiting partner sign-off'. Across the live event log, 2 cases show this repeated-review pattern. The review is being held more than once and is not reaching a completed, signed-off outcome on the first pass. Root cause: First-pass client reviews are not being brought to a conclusion — they stall waiting for partner sign-off and are handed to a different consultant, so the review has to be repeated rather than confirmed and closed.

evidence.label: avg_delay_days
evidence.detail: measured across 3 case(s) at Client Review

recommended_action: Make the first Client Review a confirm-and-close step by preparing sign-off in advance and keeping the review with one owner.
action_steps: Circulate a short findings summary to the client and the signing partner two working days before the review so the meeting confirms conclusions rather than uncovering new questions.
Assign a single named consultant as owner of each engagement's review, so it is not re-run by a second person when it stalls.
Build the partner sign-off into the review itself — have the partner attend or pre-approve against the summary so the case does not sit 'awaiting sign-off' after the meeting.
Only re-book a second review by explicit exception, with a recorded reason, rather than as the default when sign-off is outstanding.

Root cause: The most plausible cause is that each proposal is being drafted and progressed as bespoke work with no standard template or defined hand-off, so preparation and internal review stretch out before the proposal is issued.

title: Cases loop back to Delivery
summary: Two cases in the live event log passed through the Delivery stage more than once, meaning work that had already been delivered was sent back into Delivery. The evidence shows the same handler completing delivery on separate dates with differing statuses, consistent with delivered work being reopened rather than closed out cleanly. The volume is small (2 affected cases), so this is an early or low-frequency signal rather than a systemic breakdown. Root cause: Delivered work is being reopened because the agreed scope or client expectations shift after delivery begins, and there is no gate that locks scope before work restarts.
